extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, and law students (patent law practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: An index of U.S. patent-case doctrines and legal standards for patentability, infringement, remedies, re-issue, licensing, and related procedural/equitable rules used to evaluate and apply patent rights. The page lists discrete legal principles drawn from case excerpts (tests, presumptions, and procedural limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret use not a bar to patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Secret use not prior use; secret use no bar to patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears repeatedly: secret/exclusive private uses generally do not invalidate a later patent (see citations e.g., 'Secret use no bar to patent', 'Secret use not prior use').

rubrics_metrics.name: License to use may be restricted
rubrics_metrics.description: License to use may be restricted by the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties may contractually limit the scope of a license (territory, conditions); restrictions affect rights of licensee and downstream vendees.

rubrics_metrics.name: License transferability is contractual
rubrics_metrics.description: License transferable or not, as parties choose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a license can be assigned depends on the license terms and parties' agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: License to make/sell with restrictions carries right to use with restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: A license to make and sell with restrictions carries the right to use with corresponding restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A licensing grant that limits making/selling also limits the implicit right to use; enforcement follows the agreed restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee may restrict use by grantee's vendees to territory
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentee may restrict use of articles by his grantee's vendees to certain territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner can impose territorial limits on downstream purchasers via licensing/assignment terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign use not prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign use is not prior use for U.S. patentability purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses outside the U.S. do not automatically defeat U.S. patentability under the public use/novelty doctrines cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account incidental to discovery or injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: An accounting is incident to a discovery or injunction and is not ordered without them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable accounting remedies (profits, accounts) are ancillary to injunctive or discovery relief and are not granted separately without appropriate equitable grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings not sufficient reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings may not be sufficient reduction to practice if no model or other concrete proof exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no model/demonstration exists, drawings alone may not prove actual reduction to practice; extrinsic evidence may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity of designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity of designs is a determinative issue in design-patent disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts apply specific tests for design identity (inspection, comparison) and consider embodiment in drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal jurisdiction over title-to-patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal courts have jurisdiction over cases involving the title to a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When patent title is directly in issue, federal jurisdiction generally exists; related caveats and limits cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue of patent for composition may cover ingredients
rubrics_metrics.description: A re-issue of a patent for a composition may cover ingredients (i.e., details of composition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue can correct/clarify composition claims subject to re-issue limits (must relate to originally patented subject matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-owners' relation and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Relation and accountability of co-owners of a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-owners have fiduciary/obligatory relationships affecting exploitation and enforcement; courts consider division of rights and accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and requisites of inventive skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature of inventive skill required; requisites to patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentability requires more than ordinary mechanical skill in many contexts; courts analyze inventive/conceptual contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court discretion on preliminary injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Court is at liberty to grant or refuse preliminary injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting a preliminary injunction is discretionary; courts balance factors (likelihood of success, irreparable harm, public interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use defined as use without restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Public use is a use without restrictions, regardless of whether physically public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A use that is unrestricted (even if not in a public place) can constitute public use and bar patenting unless within experimental-use exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental use not public use (exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental use, even when public and producing profit, is not necessarily public use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities for testing/experimentation by or under control of inventor may be excluded from 'public use' analysis if genuinely experimental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement profits can exist despite unprofitable business
rubrics_metrics.description: Profits may accrue from infringements even though the whole business is unprofitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damages/awardable profits are measured by infringing activity, not overall profitability of the infringer's enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert evidence may aid in construing patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert evidence may aid the court in construing a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical/expert testimony helps courts interpret specifications, claims, and art understood by skilled artisans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder of improvements (claims to improvements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joinder (joining) of improvements in claims or suits is treated specially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts regulate joinder of distinct improvements to avoid multifariousness and improper aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury decides sufficiency of description; court decides sufficiency of claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Jury determines sufficiency of the description; the court determines sufficiency of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division of responsibility: factual sufficiency of disclosure may be for the jury; legal sufficiency/claim construction is for the court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of surrender and withdrawal of re-issue application
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocation of surrender and withdrawal of a re-issue application is governed by statute and case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural limits exist on withdrawing a surrendered patent and on the scope of permissible re-issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of equivalents (equivalents defined)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Equivalent' defined; the doctrine of equivalents governs when unclaimed variations infringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts define 'equivalent' contextually; use of 'equivalent' language in claims creates interpretive issues (see multiple citations defining 'equivalent').

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for identity of machines
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity of machines and tests for identity are established by specific criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparison tests (structure, function, result) are used to determine whether machines are the same for novelty/infringement analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement by using things made before patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of things made prior to the patent may constitute infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production prior to a patent does not necessarily immunize later use/sale if the acts occur after the patent grant (context-specific).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder of generic and specific claims allowed in some circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Joinder of generic and specific claims may be permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts address when a generic claim may be joined with specific claims without prejudicing clarity or statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conception, reduction to practice, and diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Conception completed and diligence in reduction to practice connect conception to patent priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority disputes consider the date of conception, reduction to practice, and reasonable diligence to file; delay by prior inventor may affect rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay by prior inventor affects rights (laches/priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of delay of a prior inventor in applying for a patent impacts priority and validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unreasonable delay or inaction by an earlier inventor can forfeit or affect rights (consider doctrines like abandonment/laches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent privilege is a conditional grant, not a contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent privilege is a conditional grant rather than a contractual right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents are statutory grants subject to conditions/limitations, not ordinary bilateral contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue confined to matters attempted in the original
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue is confined to matters attempted to be described and claimed in the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A re-issue cannot introduce entirely new subject matter beyond what was originally disclosed/attempted to be claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's decisions on re-issues may be conclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions of the Patent Office Commissioner on re-issues are afforded conclusive effect in some respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative determinations by the Commissioner may be given deference/finality on certain re-issue questions, subject to judicial review limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between art and apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts distinguish between an art (process/method) and apparatus (device/product).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different patentability and claim-drafting rules apply to processes versus apparatuses/products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use with new force or new object
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of an invention with a new force or to a new object can affect infringement/novelty analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying an old means to a new purpose may or may not be patentable depending on whether the application is new and nonobvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requisites of notice of prior publication
rubrics_metrics.description: There are legal requisites for what constitutes effective notice of a prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior publications must sufficiently describe the same invention to serve as prior art; formal notice requirements may apply in litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquiescence evidentiary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquiescence shows validity only when of considerable duration and extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term, widespread acquiescence can be evidence of patent validity (e.g., no prior challenge by others who would benefit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent construed as an entirety
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent should be construed as an entirety (specification and claims read together).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are interpreted in the context of the entire specification and prosecution history; piecemeal construction is disfavored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent amendable to perfect disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be amended to perfect the disclosure of the invention in some circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments (e.g., disclaimers) may be allowed to correct defects in disclosure, subject to re-issue and statutory limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variations in form between original and re-issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Variations in form between an original patent and its re-issue are admissible within limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor variations that do not introduce new matter may be acceptable; courts compare texts to assess identity and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successive re-issues allowable (within limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successive re-issues are allowable subject to statutory and equitable constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple re-issues may be permitted but cannot be used to enlarge monopoly improperly or introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patents issued without notice to caveator
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent issued without notice to a caveator has particular legal effects and possible challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural irregularities like failure to notify interested parties can affect later enforcement and challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent issued during interference
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent issued to one contestant during an interference proceeding affects rights in the interference context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interference practice and outcomes can be impacted when a patent issues to one party while contest remains unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim must distinguish old and new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim must distinguish the old (prior art) from the new (invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should clearly indicate the novel contribution relative to prior art; description must enable this distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearness of description is necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearness of the description in the specification is necessary for validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications must be clear enough to enable those skilled in the art to make and use the invention; ambiguity can be fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of composition must be sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of chemical or composition inventions must be sufficiently detailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition disclosures require detail on components/ratios and how to make/use to satisfy enablement and written-description requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patented article lawfully sold released from monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: A patented article lawfully sold is released from the monopoly for that specific article (exhaustion/first-sale doctrine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A purchaser may use or resell an item they lawfully bought; but rights vary for repair/reconstruction and downstream restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee enjoined for breaching license conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A licensee can be enjoined if he breaks the conditions of the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts enforce express license terms and may grant injunctions to enforce breached conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conception without reduction and abandoned experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Conception without reduction to practice and abandoned experiments have limited weight for patent rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception must be corroborated and connected to reduction to practice (or diligent steps) to establish priority; abandoned experiments generally insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement by making, sale, or use
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement may occur by making, selling, or using the patented invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three types of acts can constitute infringement depending on claim scope and territorial jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express license expires with the term of the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: An express license's enforceability may end with the patent term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licenses tied to the patent grant may expire when the patent expires unless otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiments not prior use (repeated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments or experimental uses are not necessarily prior use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental activities aimed at development or testing typically do not start the statutory bar period if they fall within recognized exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of profits where invention gives infringing article market value
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the invention gives the infringing article its market value, profits are measured accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may measure infringer's profits based on the added value attributable to the patented feature rather than total sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional power over patent privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress has power to create and define the patent privilege (scope and limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory framework establishes the patent monopoly and its public-policy limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages rules and measure at law
rubrics_metrics.description: There are established legal rules for measuring damages at law in patent cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damages may be measured by lost sales, price differentials, reasonable royalties, or other equitable analyses per precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringer losses not deductible from profits award
rubrics_metrics.description: Losses of infringers are not generally deducted from profits computed on infringing sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profits attributable to infringement are calculated without subtracting infringer's broader business losses in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of U.S. patent may be limited by foreign patents
rubrics_metrics.description: The term of a U.S. patent can be limited in effect by foreign patents in some contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign filings/rights can affect practical rights/exploitation abroad and can complicate remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of patent permissible within limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be amended subject to statutory constraints and equitable review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments (re-issue, disclaimer) allowed to correct errors but cannot expand or introduce new matter beyond original disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent privilege intended to secure disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent privilege is intended to secure public disclosure of inventions in exchange for monopoly rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quid pro quo underlies enablement/written-description requirements and limits on claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity in description detrimental
rubrics_metrics.description: Ambiguity in the description of the specification can defeat or limit a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications must be sufficiently precise; ambiguous wording can narrow claim scope or lead to invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivocal words (like 'equivalent') in claims are scrutinized
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivocal terms such as 'equivalent' in claims are subject to close judicial scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of imprecise catch-all language can create indefiniteness or interpretive issues; courts look to context and prosecution history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional claiming is recognized but governed by limits and tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims reciting functions must still satisfy statutory requirements and be clear to those skilled in the art; courts have special scrutiny for pure functional claiming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer needed only when excess is material
rubrics_metrics.description: A disclaimer is needed only when the excess (over breadth) is a material part of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-material overbreadth may be cured without disclaimers in some cases; material excess requires express disclaimers to avoid invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural law of a machine (structure controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: The structural law (structure) of a machine is central to patent analysis of machine claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts evaluate the structural elements and their cooperation in machines to determine novelty and infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties may concede priority by agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have power to concede priority by agreement in interference/priority contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements between contestants can resolve priority disputes subject to statutory constraints and public policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee's rights to patents
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee's right to patents depends on employment agreements and statutory principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventorship, assignment, and employer-employee relationships determine who owns patent rights and enforcement standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract theory of patent privilege (historical doctrine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent privilege has been analogized to a conditional grant rather than a pure contract (historical doctrinal note).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Older cases discuss patents in contract-like terms but modern analysis focuses on statutory grant and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection as test of design
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspection is the test of whether a design is identical or infringed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual inspection and comparison of overall appearance are primary in design-patent disputes (with supporting tests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of designs and embodiment in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Designs can be combined and must be embodied clearly in drawings to be protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents rely on drawings to show claimed appearance; combinations of designs require clear depiction and claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement by co-owners
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-owners may infringe a patent by unauthorized acts; co-ownership does not immunize infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership structure affects standing and liability; co-owner exploitation may still give rise to infringement claims among co-owners or third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquiescence as proof of validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquiescence (e.g., long-standing lack of challenge) may be evidence of validity but requires substantial duration/extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License-taking, failure to challenge by rival parties, and long acceptance can bolster presumptions of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of defendant's own patent on disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant's own patent can affect remedies and defenses in an infringement suit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing patents, cross-licenses, or prior art patents by defendant are relevant to invalidity/noninfringement defenses and equitable relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description construed with other parts of the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and description are construed together with other parts of the specification and relevant records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation is holistic; prosecution history and specification language influence claim scope and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents not granted to importers (historical principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally patents are granted to inventors, not importers (historical principle noted in cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership/entitlement rules historically favor inventors; importation without invention usually not patentable basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement: description intelligible to skilled artisans
rubrics_metrics.description: The description must be intelligible to those skilled in the art (enablement requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications should enable a person of ordinary skill to make and use the invention without undue experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Description and Claim
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification's description and the claim have distinct purposes: disclosure vs. defining monopoly scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts analyze the description to interpret claims, but claims define legal rights; both must be coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to all species of a genus
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee has rights to all species of his disclosed genus under certain doctrines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad genus claims can be allowed where the specification supports coverage of all species, but written-description and enablement constrain breadth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent covers all modes of embodiment
rubrics_metrics.description: A valid patent may cover all modes of embodiment of the claimed invention disclosed in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts interpret claims to encompass the disclosed embodiments; abstract principles without reduction are not patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle or abstraction not patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere principle, idea, or abstraction is not patentable absent reduction to practice or specific application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims to pure principles are invalid; patentability requires application/embodiment or reduction to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Result or effect per se not patentable
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere result or effect is not patentable without concrete means to achieve it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents must claim concrete means/structure/process rather than abstract desired results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict construction of letters-patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are subject to strict construction (narrow interpretation) in some doctrines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may construe patent claims narrowly against patentees when statutory or equitable reasons require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer liability for contractor's infringing acts limited
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer is not necessarily liable for infringing acts of an independent contractor without specific conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vicarious/new liability depends on control, agency, and contractual terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of remedy at law bars equitable relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Where damages at law are adequate, equitable remedies (like injunctions) may be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts consider adequacy of monetary compensation when deciding injunctive relief in patent cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice required for some priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction to practice can be necessary to establish priority in certain contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive or actual reduction to practice plus diligence often required for priority; incomplete efforts may not suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvements may be patentable if they meet novelty and inventive-step requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts analyze whether an improvement is more than obvious variation of known elements and whether it produces a new result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages measured by lost sales or advantage of patented feature
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages may be measured by plaintiff's lost sales or the advantage conferred by the patented feature over open inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple damages measures exist; courts choose the appropriate metric based on causation and available evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue cannot be used to enlarge claims improperly
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-issue will not be granted to improperly enlarge claims beyond original scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue is remedial but cannot expand monopoly beyond what was claimed/disclosed originally; unreasonable delay in seeking re-issue can invalidate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay in seeking re-issue may forfeit right
rubrics_metrics.description: Unreasonable delay (e.g., over two years in some cases) in seeking re-issue may forfeit right to re-issue or render it invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness and reasonableness of delay are considered by courts when assessing re-issue validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision of Commissioner on re-issue final as to fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Office Commissioner's decision on fraud in re-issue proceedings is in many cases final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fraud findings in re-issue may be given deference to the administrative determination, subject to narrow judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product protection may continue absent machine patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A product may be protected by its patent even if the related machine patent has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different patents (machine vs product/process) provide different scopes and durations; product protection can persist if separately patented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of vendee: repair vs rebuild
rubrics_metrics.description: A purchaser (vendee) of a patented article may repair it but generally cannot rebuild it (distinction between permissible repair and unlawful reconstruction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible repair preserves the functioning of a sold article; rebuilding to create a new article may be an infringing reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option of licensor to sue for infringement or on contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensor may choose to sue for infringement or for breach of contract as an option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of remedy (infringement suit vs contractual suit) can affect available relief and damages calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent extended to cover all modes of embodiment (reiterated)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent may be interpreted to extend to all modes of embodiment disclosed or fairly within claim scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim scope covers disclosed embodiments and equivalents subject to statutory limits; abstract principles alone are excluded.
